page: Microsoft Azure FX4ms_v2 is a high-frequency compute and memory-dense virtual machine powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance includes 260 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It features 84.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB per vCPU, while offering no bundled local storage and no hardware accelerators.

The 4.2 GHz clock speed drives exceptional single-threaded execution, as demonstrated by top-decile Geekbench single-core scores of 2353.0 and strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance relies on 2 physical cores with 4 threads, multi-core throughput is constrained, falling into lower benchmark percentiles for stress-ng multi-core loads and multi-threaded compilation. Memory subsystem testing shows capable cached read bandwidth, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidth register in lower tiers.

The FX4ms_v2 provides an asymmetrical architecture suited for single-threaded or license-bound enterprise applications requiring large in-memory footprints. The high memory density makes it effective for medium-scale in-memory caching, relational database workloads with high per-core licensing costs, and Electronic Design Automation batch tasks. Because local storage is absent, deployments must rely on network-attached storage solutions.
description: Microsoft Azure FX4ms_v2 is a memory-dense, high-frequency compute instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by a 260 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions. It is provisioned with 84.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 21.0 GB per core, but includes no local storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-thread performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2353.0 and strong compression throughput, though multi-core capacity remains limited by the two-core physical topology. While uncached memory bandwidth is comparatively modest, the high ratio of memory to compute cores offers clear resource efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis. The FX4ms_v2 is well configured for in-memory databases, electronic design automation, batch financial modeling, and memory-intensive enterprise applications requiring high single-core execution speed.
